interpretation: Records acceptance and evidence. Neither completion nor an AI assessment establishes correctness, safety, or independent review.
objective:
ACCEPT or DECLINE this judging mandate. Read the complete SQF below. ACCEPT only if the question can be judged fairly after its deadline by independent researchers who may use different sources and methods, and DECLINE if it cannot. If you DECLINE, return a corrected SQF in the same report.

SQF
§question Will the S&P 500 index close higher on Tuesday 20 October 2026 than it closed on Friday 16 October 2026?
§rule Return YES if the official S&P 500 closing level on 2026-10-20 is strictly greater than the official closing level on 2026-10-16; NO if it is lower or equal; INVALID only if either regular US trading session is cancelled.
§source S&P Dow Jones Indices official close (spglobal.com/spdji), cross-checked with a major market-data aggregator
§deadline 2026-10-20T21:30:00Z, after the US close
§resolution subjective expert judgment under this accepted mandate; researchers choose their own sources, methods and reasoning
§why it matters many people hold savings in index funds; near-term direction is genuinely uncertain, which makes the disagreement between independent views informative

submissions.summary:
**Verdict: ACCEPT.** I wrote the report to `artifacts/acceptance.md` and added a short `README.md` in the repo root. I haven't committed anything.

- **Why it can be judged fairly:** The outcome is binary and comes from one comparison of two public closing levels. YES means the 20 October close is strictly higher than the 16 October close. A tie counts as NO. Independent researchers can verify it from many sources after the deadline, whatever their own view of market direction.
- **Calendar check:** 16 October 2026 is a Friday and 20 October is a Tuesday. The 21:30Z deadline falls about 90 minutes after the US close, which is 20:00Z while US daylight time runs. I did not confirm against the NYSE holiday calendar that neither date is a market holiday.
- **Not checked:** I did not retrieve any index levels, and the report doesn't predict the outcome.
- **Inference to note:** The `§resolution` line says "subjective expert judgment", but the rule itself is mechanical. I read it as meaning researchers choose their own sources and methods, while the result still follows the comparison in `§rule`. I also read "S&P 500 index" as the price index, not total return.
- **Suggested edits:** These are optional, and I did not issue a corrected SQF. Specify the price index, say that the S&P DJI official close prevails if sources disagree, and reword `§resolution` as above.
